attempts.label: CRCNS:ia-1
attempts.entry_title: Burst coding in locust auditory receptors (Eyherabide et al. 2008)
attempts.summary: Most of the paper's tested findings on burst coding held up in this data, but its session counts and the share of information carried by bursts did not. Its threshold model could not be tested because Data1 holds no thresholds. Held: bursts are less correlated than single spikes, burst probability follows stimulus statistics, burst-triggered stimulus averages differ by burst length, and their latency falls with length. Table 1's counts did not reproduce, probably because Data1 gives 115 sessions against the paper's 86 and does not mark which were kept. Information per burst rising with length held only partly, since estimator bias is of the order of the rise.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Eyherabide, Rokem, Herz and Samengo (2008) on CRCNS data set ia-1, which holds the spike times of locust auditory receptor cells under amplitude-modulated noise (Data1) and the stimuli. It identifies bursts from the spike-train correlation function, counts them per stimulus protocol, computes the information carried by bursts of each size and by the direct method, and the burst-triggered averages of the stimulus. The cells' thresholds, which the paper's model needs, are not in the data set.

outcomes.statement: Thirty-seven receptor cells were recorded from 23 animals, giving 132 sessions, of which 86 met the firing-rate and stationarity conditions; each stimulus was repeated 98 to 503 times, 172 on average.
outcomes.source: Materials and Methods, Electrophysiology and stimulus design, paragraphs 1, 4 and 5
outcomes.quote: Thirty-seven receptor cells were recorded, from 23 animals. Each cell was tested with two or more stimuli, resulting in 132 data sets in total ... There were 86 out of 132 data sets that fulfilled these two conditions ... N repetitions of each stimulus were presented, with N ranging between 98 and 503 (average 172)
outcomes.notes: The 116 sessions of the seven protocols come from 37 cells (rows of singlecells.txt) recorded on 23 dates; the 122 Gaussian AM sessions of any cutoff are within 10% of the paper's 132 (all 150 Data1 sessions are not). Under the criterion's readings the SD < 35 Hz condition keeps 115 of the 116 (113 with a 100 Hz target, reading b; 116 with whole-trial rates), against 86; over the 115 trials range from 69 (outside 98 +/- 9.8) to 503 and average 160.3, and the mean trial-to-trial SD of the rate is 6.48 Hz (within 6 +/- 0.6). Selection (c), which also leaves out the 9 sessions under 98 trials and the off-line sorted sessions, keeps 89 sessions with 98 to 503 trials (mean 168.7) and a mean SD of 6.00 Hz, within tolerance, but they come from 29 cells on 18 dates, outside 37 +/- 3.7 and 23 +/- 2.3 (the 37 cells and 23 dates hold over all seven-protocol sessions); it is not a reading of the criterion, which defines the selection by the rate conditions, and its fewest trials are 98 by construction, so it does not decide this outcome. The trial blocks were checked: late spikes (up to 2.76 s) occur only in off-line sorted sessions, in the pause, no block restarts its times or holds twice the usual spike count, and the data set's firing_rates file gives the same trial counts in 136 of 138 files.
deviations: Data1 does not record the animal; the 23 recording dates stand in for the 23 animals, assuming one animal per date.

outcomes.statement: The information carried by each n-burst increases with n; every bursting session has a significantly positive slope of I_n(1) against n, with an average slope of 1.5 bits (SD 0.7 bits) over 59 bursting cells.

Burst identification takes the first peak as the largest value of C_s below 5 ms (peak reading b), the first local minimum after it that differs significantly from it (minimum reading a), and the error bar with sigma the SD of the product terms of Eq. 1 and N their number (reading a). Assumed because the first local maximum (reading a) falls on edge effects of the refractory plateau, where C_s has no spike pairs, which the Methods say the criteria reject (Burst identification, paragraph 5), and leaves 11 of 89 sessions bursting; started after the plateau (peak reading c, added after the first verification) it leaves 61, near the 64 of the main reading; with N the number of trials no session bursts; the main reading gives an error bar of 2.6% of the span of C_s, near the paper's 3.4% (paragraph 6). The notebook shows every combination.

outcomes.statement: The threshold-linear model with refractoriness reproduces the coding trends of the data, at single-cell and population level, though it is less precise in time than the real cells.
outcomes.source: Results, Quantitative description of the information transmitted by bursts, paragraph 8; Figure 7, right half; Figures 8C and 9D
outcomes.quote: A comparison between the left and right panels of Figure 7 reveals that the model reproduces the general trends observed in the experimental data, both at the single-cell and population level.
outcomes.notes: Depends on model-matches-classification, blocked because Data1 holds no thresholds s_TH.

findings.statement: The paper keeps 86 of 132 sessions by a trial-to-trial rate SD below 35 Hz and a rate near 100 Hz. In Data1 the SD rule keeps 115 of the 116 sessions of the paper's seven protocols (and all 116 with whole-trial rates), and nothing marks which sessions the paper kept. Leaving out also the 9 sessions with fewer than 98 trials and the off-line sorted sessions keeps 89, with 47, 6, 7, 7, 8, 7 and 7 per protocol against Table 1's 43, 6, 7, 7, 8, 7 and 8, and bursting sessions per protocol equal to Table 1's in six of seven, which suggests the paper used only on-line sorted sessions; the paper does not say so.

Data1 holds no threshold, best frequency or f-I measurement for its cells, though the paper's model (Eq. 2) uses the measured threshold s_TH and the descriptor says the best frequency was determined from f-I curves.

Data1 does not record the animal; the paper's 23 animals can only be matched to the 23 recording dates of the seven-protocol sessions by assuming one animal per date. Two experiments (03-01-15-aa, 03-06-27-ae) are missing from singlecells.txt.

28 sessions use the stimuli gaussModality_co200 and lmd_co200 and 6 use cutoffs of 50 and 1600 Hz; the descriptor does not describe these stimuli and the paper does not use them. 28 sessions sorted off-line have no header, so their target rate and pause are not recorded, and in 25 of them each trial block runs on into the pause (spikes up to 2.76 s), which the descriptor does not mention. The file Data1/firing_rates is not described; it gives each spike file's trial count and a rate with a +/- value of 57 to 189 Hz that is not the trial-to-trial SD of the rate.

The descriptor says the 1 s trials number 98 to 533; the files hold 69 to 503. The intensity in three trial headers differs from cell.dat by more than 1 dB (03-04-11-aa sig2, 03-04-16-ae sig2, 03-04-23-ae sig1, up to 6.6 dB), and six sessions of 03-01-30-ad, 03-02-25-ac and 03-02-25-aj had 450 ms pauses where the paper states 700 ms.

Questions for the paper's authors. (1) Burst identification; which maximum is the first peak of C_s (the first local maximum falls on edge effects of the refractory plateau and leaves 11 of 89 sessions bursting, 61 when the search starts after the plateau, the largest value below 5 ms 64), and what sigma and N are in Delta = sigma / sqrt(N) (the product terms and their number give 2.6% of the span when tau = 0 is left out of the span; N the number of trials gives no bursting session). (2) Which rule, besides the rate SD, removed the sessions not among the 86; whether the sessions with spikes detected off-line and those with fewer than 98 trials were left out. (3) How events were formed for the jitter (Rokem et al., 2006). (4) Whether the mean stimulus was subtracted before summing 1BTAs in Eq. 15. (5) What separates a peak of C_s for the multi-modal and single-peaked shapes of Figure 3. (6) Whether the maximum of the nBTA that gives tau_n was searched before burst onset, and how many bursts of each n a session needed. (7) Whether I_n(1) was corrected for the bias of the plug-in estimate, whose bias here is of the order of its rise with n.
The paper counts bursting sessions three ways, 63 with n > 1 in Table 1, 59 bursting cells for Figure 7B and 58 bursting sessions for Figure 8, without saying why.

entries.name: eyherabide-2008
entries.title: Burst coding in locust auditory receptors (Eyherabide et al. 2008)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Eyherabide, Rokem, Herz and Samengo (2008) on CRCNS data set ia-1, which holds the spike times of locust auditory receptor cells under amplitude-modulated noise (Data1) and the stimuli. It identifies bursts from the spike-train correlation function, counts them per stimulus protocol, computes the information carried by bursts of each size and by the direct method, and the burst-triggered averages of the stimulus. The cells' thresholds, which the paper's model needs, are not in the data set.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Eyherabide et al. (2008) from CRCNS ia-1
